image:image.image:title: Why design thinking struggles to create repeat engagement
image:image.image:caption: the design is most useful when it clarifies ownership, trade-offs, and follow-through in day-to-day execution.

image:image.image:title: Gamification fails when it turns into surveillance or burnout
image:image.image:caption: Disney's electronic whip, FarmVille's withering crops, and Yahoo Answers' point system share a structural failure: each was designed around what's easy to measure, not around what sustains the behavior the designers actually wanted.

image:image.image:title: Why delight belongs inside the core loop
image:image.image:caption: Users apologizing to their own browser tabs were revealing something analytics dashboards miss: a product can be functionally complete and emotionally broken at the same time. The design problem isn't clutter - it's what the clutter makes people feel.
